title: Since 0.12.0 keyboard input does not work (macOS)
body:
For bug reports, the following information can help speed up the process. Please
describe the bug that you have found and what you would expect to happen
instead.

### System

OS: macOS 12.6.3 (21G419)
Version: alacritty 0.12.0 (5a72819)

### Logs

Font/Terminal size: [Alacritty-75137.log](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/files/11068753/Alacritty-75137.log)


When I start Alacritty using the App Icon or Spotlight, the keyboard input (except Enter, Escape, Backspace and maybe some more) does not work. When I start Alacritty from Terminal it works just fine. Also tested using the default config.

comments.author: participant19
comments.body:
For those text input in Alacritty works for, do you have more than one input method?

I only have one keyboard layout, but do have Fig and its input method (for the completion popup).
Whenever I uninstall the Fig input method, Alacritty works.
When I re-install it, it breaks again.
For uninstalling I need to restart Alacritty, but when installing the Fig input method it breaks immediately.
It's still temporarily resolved by changing keyboard layout, as others have mentioned.

Edit:
Alacritty v0.11.0 works for me, but Alacritty v0.12.0-rc1 does not.

I've tested on both an intel 2019 MacBook Pro, and an M1 2022 MacBook Pro, if that'd matter.
Both are on macOS Ventura.

Edit 2:
After a bisect, https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/commit/1c878a0476257d328113efcd7088f1aa53f42e56 is the commit where it starts breaking for me.

Edit 3:
I tried bisecting both winit and Alacritty alongside each other, to try and get a rough pointer on where it happens.
As the commit message in my 2nd edit is an update to winit 0.28.0, that's what I picked as a bad commit.

Eventually I got to the https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/commit/3fd73848dd36cc051cc3a0bec305ba8b2a117145 commit, where it started breaking again.
Reverting [this line](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/3fd73848dd36cc051cc3a0bec305ba8b2a117145/src/platform_impl/macos/view.rs#L428), specifically, it starts working again.
With the other change/added line in that commit, it still works.
This was also tested against Alacrittys latest master, which works with that line reverted.

That's about as helpful as I could possibly be, unfortunately, as I'm not super-familiar in this area, nor fluent in Rust.

comments.author: participant19
comments.body:
I've done some more testing.

Irrespective of layout I've tested (US, US International, British, Canadian, Finnish, Swedish, Norwegian, German, ...), using special characters like `´`, `¨`, `~` will make it possible to type anything again.
So I don't need to switch layouts, or so - just tap one of them and all keys are again available for me.

I only ever have a single layout added at a time, but always with Figs input method installed.
All of them works correctly if I uninstall the Fig input method.
Contrary to what I mentioned before, I do have to restart Alacritty after re-installing Figs input method.

-----
Rust, developing terminals, IME, etc, isn't really my cup of tea [yet], but I tried poking around the code a bit, testing things.

<details>
<summary>I wrote down the things I tested, if it's of use to anyone</summary>

<details>
<summary>Steps I used to install and compile things on macOS</summary>

I clone both winit and Alacritty, alongside each other.
I then switch the winit reference in both alacritty/alacritty/Cargo.toml and alacritty/alacritty_config/Cargo.toml from
```toml
winit = { version = "0.28.2", default-features = false, features = ["serde"] }
```

to
```toml
winit = { path = "../../winit", default-features = false, features = ["serde"] }
```

Then do the changes I'd like to test, and follow the manual installation instructions outlined [here](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/blob/master/INSTALL.md#macos).
Which really is just running `make app` in the alacritty directory.
To clean up between each test, I use `make clean`, then `make app` again.
The compiled app can be found inside the alacritty/target/release/osx directory.
</details>

<details>
<summary>What I tested</summary>
Because these two lines ([1](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/blob/ead65221ebe06ff5689e65b866d735d4365d0e9e/alacritty/src/display/window.rs#L176), [2](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/blob/ead65221ebe06ff5689e65b866d735d4365d0e9e/alacritty/src/display/window.rs#L179)) were added in the Alacritty [commit I linked above](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/issues/6817#issuecomment-1510439015), I tried commenting them out.
But it still didn't work.

While [this line](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/blob/ead65221ebe06ff5689e65b866d735d4365d0e9e/alacritty/src/display/window.rs#L175) wasn't changed in that commit, I tested to disable IME by setting it to false.
That did make it work.

There's no doubt it's about IME, which is why I was poking around the relevant lines linked above.
But nothing I do in Alacritty itself seems to fix it.

Back to winit, I proceeded to revert [this line](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/249609889029af3e5ec19afbd02464e11a265378/src/platform_impl/macos/view.rs#L432) again.
While far-fetched in this case, I've seen some weird stuff before..
So I tried calling `self.hasMarkedText()` before the loop, to ensure it's not something being done in that function.
That does make it work, as one would expect.
<details>
<summary>Snippet used</summary>

```rust
self.hasMarkedText();

// Commit only if we have marked text.
if self.is_ime_enabled() && !is_control {
    self.queue_event(WindowEvent::Ime(Ime::Preedit(String::new(), None)));
    self.queue_event(WindowEvent::Ime(Ime::Commit(string)));
    self.state.ime_state = ImeState::Commited;
}
```
</details>

I'm not sure if text should be marked at this stage, or not (or what it means).
Or why it's considered marked when starting Alacritty from another terminal.

</details>

</details>
